corrections.text: Can the Supreme Court reduce the sentence on the basis of a compromise in an offence under Section 326 IPC that cannot be compounded under Section 320?
corrections.reason: Q06 said Section 325. Section 325 IPC is compoundable with the court's permission under Section 320(2); the landmark (Nanda Gopalan) concerns Sections 324 and 326, which are not in Section 320. The old passages were found with a section search on 325, so they are not a fair pool for the corrected question: Q06v2 needs a new pool and new marks.

corrections.rewrite_v2: Whether a court can permit compounding of, or reduce the sentence in view of a compromise between the parties for, the offence of voluntarily causing grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means (Section 326 IPC), which is not compoundable under Section 320 CrPC.
corrections.reason: The v1 hand rewrite called voluntarily causing grievous hurt (Section 325) 'not compoundable under Section 320'. The question text itself is unchanged (it only says 'grievous hurt' and 'non-compoundable'), so Q05's marks stand; versions C and F for Q05 were run on the old rewrite and need re-running and re-marking.

new_topics.notes: Mohan Lal v State of Punjab (2018), the decision Mukesh Singh overruled, IS in the collection and the index (doc 1000250931, titled 'MOHANLAL versus THE STATE OF PUNJAB'), so its own passages, which state the view the Constitution Bench rejected, can appear in a search: this is a direct currency trap. (A note of 2026-10-08 said it was missing; that was wrong, my search had split the name 'Mohan Lal' into two words.) Mukesh Singh also quotes the overruled view.
